correctness.rationale: Hilbert's projective degree formula for three-part binary coincident-root loci is 6abc if a,b,c distinct, 3a²b when exactly two parts agree, and a³ if all equal. The strata (1,1,d−2) and (1,2,d−3) show the gcd for d>=6 divides 3 gcd(d−2,4), hence 12. A complete split by d mod4 shows common two-adic valuation 0 (odd), 1 (d=0 mod4), or 2 (d=2 mod4), with explicit witness degrees attaining each bound. A split by nu_3(d) shows the three-factor disappears exactly when the all-equal stratum has d/3 not divisible by 3, i.e. nu_3(d)=1; otherwise common v3=1 via witness strata. d=3,4,5 are checked directly. Independently enumerated all 3,482,597 three-part partitions for 3<=d<=500 and recovered G_d=2^alpha 3^beta throughout; the unlimited conclusion follows from the divisibility proof.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS: Hilbert's explicit degree for each partition is old, and a published Resultary result classifies minima and maxima over the EXACT same three-part family. Neither supplies the gcd over every stratum (the common prime/power invariant), because extremal values do not determine a gcd. Fehér–Némethi–Rimányi and Lee–Sturmfels treat geometry and pointwise formulas; no uniform arithmetic gcd law was found in their inspected material. The result does not pretend Hilbert's degree formula is new.

value.rationale: PASS. The family of all three-dimensional coincident root strata is canonical, and the greatest common divisor of their projective degrees is a natural global divisibility invariant controlling simultaneous arithmetic properties of generic intersection counts. The two-prime law and sharp disappearance of the 3-factor at nu_3(d)=1 are exact, nonobvious from just the extrema, and self-contained; no larger theorem is required for this precise unknown natural invariant to be worthwhile.
residual_risks: Result may be relatively elementary given Hilbert’s classical formula; value rests on complete common-divisibility classification, not on inventing Hilbert geometry.
